name: Termly
description: Termly is a data privacy compliance platform for consent management, website cookie scanning, and legal policy generation. Organizations use it to configure consent banners, monitor cookies, publish policies, and support privacy requests.
agentUseSummary: Connect one Termly account and one selected website with a customer-owned partner API key pair. Agents can inspect a redacted website compliance summary and bounded banner settings; other websites, visitor consent data, cookie detail, contacts, snippets, documents, collaborators, writes, paging, and raw API access are blocked.

credentialRequirements.name: TERMLY_PUBLIC_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: Termly partner public key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Termly manually issues the partner public key. Relay encrypts it server-side.

credentialRequirements.name: TERMLY_PRIVATE_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: Termly partner private key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Termly manually issues the partner private key. Relay encrypts it and uses it only for HMAC request signing.

credentialRequirements.name: TERMLY_ACCOUNT_ID
credentialRequirements.label: Termly account ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: The exact acct_ account identifier allowed by the partner key.

credentialRequirements.name: TERMLY_WEBSITE_ID
credentialRequirements.label: Selected Termly website ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: The one web_ website Relay may inspect.

capabilities.label: Read website status
capabilities.description: Read one selected website's redacted compliance and scan-status summary.

capabilities.label: Read banner status
capabilities.description: Read one selected website's bounded consent-banner configuration summary.

allowed.label: Read selected website status
allowed.description: Read one selected website's redacted compliance and scan-status summary.

allowed.label: Read selected banner status
allowed.description: Read one selected website's bounded consent-banner configuration summary.

blocked.label: Expose private compliance data
blocked.description: Partner keys, WordPress API keys, company contacts, code snippets, consent records, visitor identifiers, cookie details, documents, and collaborator data are excluded.

blocked.label: Mutate Termly configuration
blocked.description: Website, banner, cookie, theme, document, scan, collaborator, and consent mutations are blocked.

blocked.label: Use broad Termly access
blocked.description: Account-wide listing, other websites, paging, scrolling, arbitrary queries, raw paths, batch requests, redirects, and export are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Read Only
approvalProfiles.description: Read status for one selected website and its banner; private data and mutations remain blocked.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway attaches the encrypted partner key pair server-side and mounts exactly two selected-website read tools.
Railway attaches the encrypted partner key pair server-side and mounts exactly two selected-website read tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Termly manually issues partner public/private API keys and directs integrators to request a separate test account. No authorized partner keys, account, selected website, or test account is available in this worker lane.
providerSetup.nextAction: An authorized organization must obtain Termly partner API access, connect its encrypted key pair, account ID, and one selected website through Relay, then validate signing, redaction, replacement, disconnect, post-disconnect denial, and both selected-website reads in Fairfax before live use.

evidence.supports: Termly documents its REST partner API and says API key pairs are issued manually through its agency program.
Termly documents the fixed HTTPS api.termly.io host, timestamped TermlyV1 signatures, query model, and live-account/test-account constraint.
Termly's official example documents the public/private key derivation, HMAC-SHA256 canonical request, account ID, website ID, and fixed API origin.
Termly documents GET /v1/websites with exact account and website IDs and response fields including sensitive keys, contacts, and code snippets that Relay removes.
Termly documents GET banner configuration for exact account and website IDs, including consent-banner display and regional settings.
